text: IEEE 754 breaks ties by rounding to even rather than always up. Why?
choices: It matches the convention taught in schools
Always rounding halves up biases every tie the same way, and the biases accumulate into a drift
It guarantees the result is always exact
Rounding to even is faster in hardware
explanation: Splitting ties between up and down lets errors tend to cancel across a long computation instead of compounding. The school convention is exactly the one being rejected. Nothing here makes a result exact — the value was already not representable.
